Present Perfect: Announcing News
You use the Present Perfect tense to announce past events that have current relevance.

You can use the Present Perfect tense to talk about experience.
When you use the Present Perfect tense, you think about the past and present together. There is some connection between what happened in the past and now.

The Present Perfect is used to announce news, or to focus on the current relevance of past events.
Example:
They have updated their website. = The website is now updated, and a past action has an impact on the current website's situation.

You use the Present Perfect Simple to talk about habitual actions or with state verbs, when there a connection to the present.
Example:
I've lived here for the past ten years. = I still live here now.
In that context, it is common to use the Present Perfect with time adverbs to say how long a situation has gone on up to the moment of speaking.
In our top story tonight, a study has revealed that children who own pets have less stress.
The research, which has included children from Australia to the UK, outlines the numerous benefits to pet ownership.
Moving to the kitchen, a new study has shown that drinking beetroot juice reduces high blood pressure.
The results have clearly demonstrated that a significant reduction in blood pressure can result from just one glass of the juice per day.
Most people have slowly begun to realize this fact, and have increased daily water intake.
Giving Reasons: For, In that, Insofar as, Inasmuch as

You use reason clauses to express the reasons for an action, or why a situation is the way it is.
You use words like for, in that, insofar as, or inasmuch as to introduce a reason clause to give a reason for something.

Reason clauses are subordinate to the main clause. They state the reason why things are done, or what makes a situation the way it is.
You can use for, in that, insofar as, or inasmuch as to introduce a reason clause to give a reason for something.

For has a meaning similar to because.
Example:
We must begin planning, for the future may have some unexpected turns.

In that, insofar as, inasmuch as, have similar meaning. They are quite formal, and are commonly found in writing rather than in spoken English. The clause they introduce clarifies what has been said by adding more detail and information.
Example:
The film is unusual in that it only features 2 main actors.

images.text:
Good evening, and welcome to the Fit Fifty, where we bring you fifty minutes of fitness news.

In our top story tonight, a study has revealed that children who own pets have less stress. The research, which has included children from Australia to the UK, outlines the numerous benefits to pet ownership. First and foremost, pets encourage physical activity. Most of our viewers will not find this surprising, inasmuch as dogs require daily walks. Pets also act as a kind of live-in therapist, in that they provide comfort and increase self-esteem. Last but not least, our furry companions can help to reduce stress and anxiety, as they stimulate interaction and conversation.

Moving to the kitchen, a new study has shown that drinking beetroot juice reduces high blood pressure. The landmark study, which was headed by a pharmacologist from Queen Mary University, focused on patients with hypertension. One group of patients was given a daily glass of beetroot juice, while the control group was given a placebo. The results have clearly demonstrated that a significant reduction in blood pressure can result from just one glass of the juice per day. The effect is caused by inorganic nitrate, which is contained in beetroot and other leafy vegetables, and which causes blood vessels to relax and dilate. The results are excellent insofar as they suggest that a reduction in blood pressure is possible; however, for most hypertension sufferers, a complete change in diet will also be necessary.

Our last story of the day involves another common beverage: water. For obvious reasons, water is an important part of a healthy lifestyle. Most people have slowly begun to realize this fact, and have increased daily water intake. Recent findings, however, suggest that many people may need to up their consumption even further. According to the Institute of Medicine, the suggested daily intake of water for men is three liters.

That's all for this edition of the Fit Fifty. Remember folks, stay fit and have fun!
